workflows.trigger: A user or technician needs to open, install, share, download, clone, update, or locally edit the current main Prompt Kit on a browser, phone, tablet, Windows PC, macOS, or Linux machine.
owned_scope: profile-qualified host, shell, target, and repository-path routing
read-only consumption of EndeavorEverlasting/AgentSwitchboard machine-profile and repository-family evidence
cross-device acquisition and profile-routing validator tests and reports
forbidden_scope: requiring a clone for normal browser or phone use
mutating AgentSwitchboard from a Triage acquisition lane
emitting Android or Termux shell commands as runnable Windows PowerShell commands
workflows.failure_policy: Preserve the active Triage repository, qualify current host profile and shell before emitting commands, and classify cross-profile requests as handoffs. Preserve existing checkouts and classify the failed gate by profile/shell mismatch, access mode, public browser/phone routing, device install, Windows launcher, editable Git checkout, network/authentication, origin/branch/divergence, required-file, or parity failure. Never substitute a destructive, cross-profile, or higher-friction route merely to make progress.
handoff_fields: profile-associated Triage path when local tooling is required
branch and commit when Git is used

workflows.trigger: Canonical prompts, policies, reference data, builder behavior, generator options, checked-in HTML, or Prompt Kit interaction contracts change.
workflows.failure_policy: Repair canonical sources or contract drift; never weaken parity, coverage, or interaction requirements merely to turn CI green.

workflows.trigger: Maps, workflow specifications, registries, validators, hooks, skills, reports, acquisition surfaces, or versioned domain contracts are missing, stale, or inconsistent.
workflows.failure_policy: Repair the canonical component or registry owner, add a regression test, rerun the first failing gate, then run the full harness profile.

workflows.trigger: A triage engine, workbook contract, schema, fixture, or generated artifact behavior changes.
workflows.failure_policy: Preserve protected inputs, reproduce with sanitized fixtures, repair the focused engine, and distinguish static proof from Excel or operator proof.

workflows.trigger: Work is stacked, divergent, superseded, or blocked across branches or pull requests.
workflows.failure_policy: Stop destructive integration, preserve unique work, identify the exact dependency or conflict, and provide the safest executable next action.

workflows.trigger: Prompt language changes or lazy, placeholder, observation-only, status-only, or non-executable next actions are suspected.
workflows.failure_policy: Stop on coverage or identity drift; repair canonical registry or builder ownership before interpreting language findings.

workflows.trigger: A skill lacks executable correctness, routing, regression, performance, cost, or token-efficiency evidence.
forbidden_scope: moving deterministic product behavior into prose
workflows.failure_policy: Reproduce the weakness, repair the smallest owned boundary, and rerun correctness before accepting efficiency changes.
